tasks[].recover_staged_payload.meaning: Collect the exact physical container marked staged and recovery-required at the specified pickup location.
tasks[].recover_staged_payload.precedence: Default false. True requires a nonempty payload_instance_id and payload; it never creates stock. Uses ordinary route profiles, robot compatibility and destination capacity. Waits until eligible or the original deferral deadline; excludes unconfirmed arrivals. Direct recovery only: no further automatic return or staff handoff.

tasks[].payload_instance_id.meaning: Optional identity of one physical container. Repeated use refers to that same object, not an instruction to duplicate it.
tasks[].payload_instance_id.precedence: An ordinary outbound task may first issue a previously unissued ID. Commitment claims that creation; after physical pickup or seeded storage the ID must be available at the requested source for reuse. Transit, removal and unconfirmed arrival do not permit recreation. Blank ordinary IDs receive unique generated identities. Return tasks normally require existing stock; internally generated staged and service continuations retain their specific policies.

corridors.auto_connect.meaning: Connect otherwise unconnected locations/lifts to the nearest corridor node when enabled.
corridors.auto_connect.validation: If supplied, the value must be an actual JSON boolean; strings, numbers and null are rejected by Project checks, editor loading and simulator construction before coercion.
corridors.auto_connect.limitations: Nearest-node linking is not geometric connectivity validation. New projects explicitly store false; imported omission deliberately retains runtime default true.
corridors.auto_connect.runtime_default: true when omitted in imported/raw configuration
corridors.auto_connect.editor_behaviour: New blank projects specify false. Imported configurations retain omission, so runtime true still applies.
corridors.auto_connect.precedence: Explicit JSON boolean wins. A new editor project explicitly stores false; importing a missing value does not insert that new-project default.

corridors.edges[].distance_m.validation: Raw Project checks require a finite nonnegative number if supplied. Runtime null also falls back; do not rely on direct CLI loading as schema validation.
corridors.edges[].distance_m.limitations: Explicit distance may disagree with drawing geometry. No surveyed-distance validation or acceleration model.
corridors.edges[].distance_m.runtime_default: Endpoint Euclidean distance when omitted or null
corridors.edges[].distance_m.editor_behaviour: Optional explicit distance retained on import.

corridors.edges[].width_m.precedence: Falls back to building.default_corridor_width_m; endpoint doors can reduce it.
corridors.edges[].width_m.validation: Explicit values must convert to a finite positive width; booleans, null, zero and negative values are rejected before import normalisation or simulation. Numeric strings remain accepted. Missing fields use the documented defaults.
corridors.edges[].width_m.limitations: Straight passage only: no safety margin, door height/swing/opening time or swept-footprint check. Both full incident edges inherit a door restriction. Editing controls with a 0.1 m minimum need later consistency review; imported smaller dimensions are not enlarged.
corridors.edges[].width_m.editor_behaviour: Import preserves all positive widths exactly, including below 0.1 m; missing node/edge widths receive the building defaults. Some editing controls still constrain entry to at least 0.1 m.

corridors.edges[].bidirectional.precedence: Default true; profile allowed edges still apply directionally.

corridors.edges[].bidirectional.limitations: Directional profile permissions can further restrict two-way edges. This is not a keep-right lane model.
corridors.edges[].bidirectional.editor_behaviour: Missing edge flag retained; runtime supplies true.

task_generation.categories.*.department_.meaning: Group payload override: Explicit positive minutes govern staff handling. Runtime fallback uses return delay, then global staff handling default.
task_generation.categories.*.department_.precedence: Group membership suppresses the standalone department rule, even when this group is disabled. Override replaces the category field.
task_generation.categories.*.department_.editor_behaviour: Imported omission now retains the generated-task default (false/0); new templates retain explicit staff settings.

tasks[].requires_staff.meaning: Explicit staff choice for a task; omitted permits the legacy Stores fallback.
tasks[].requires_staff.precedence: Explicit false suppresses legacy category fallback. Drop-off-zone handoffs force staff. Return tasks do not themselves allocate payload-handling staff.
tasks[].requires_staff.runtime_default: Unspecified (internal None); legacy Stores deliveries require staff, other ordinary deliveries do not.
tasks[].requires_staff.editor_behaviour: Supplied static task fields are retained. Generated rules preserve omission as well as explicit true/false.
tasks[].requires_staff.validation: Reference inputs use actual JSON booleans or omission. Broader generation/task scalar type validation remains open.
tasks[].requires_staff.limitations: Some older saved files may already contain default-inserted false values; their original intent cannot be inferred. Staff travel, shifts, capacity growth and all policy combinations require wider acceptance coverage.

task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.runtime_default: 1, coerced to an integer of at least one.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.meaning: Seeds the category pool on first use; later requests use its existing roster. Busy rosters automatically grow, so this is not a fixed capacity.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.precedence: Effective group/department override replaces the category field on generated tasks. Category-keyed pool is created on first staff booking; subsequent tasks do not reset its count or label.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.editor_behaviour: Category normalisation coerces to an integer of at least one; dialogs accept 1 to 999999 and explain automatic growth.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.validation: Reference tests use valid values. Runtime coercion is retained; comprehensive scalar rejection and inconsistent settings within a category are not validated.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_initi.limitations: Staffing sizing, not a capped queue or globally optimal roster. First booking controls pool count/name; categories do not share people through a common label. Shared batch finishes can exceed individual service duration; hours-search exhaustion remains an explicitly flagged fallback. Full roster/report reconciliation remains open.

task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.runtime_default: none; group omission inherits the category. Generated tasks carry definitions independently of staff choice and normally use fixed 09:00-17:00 weekday hours. Legacy direct tasks with no shift-time metadata retain all-day availability.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.meaning: none uses one roster; four_on_four_off_12h alternates teams A and B in four-day blocks from simulation start and sizes two teams from the peak on-shift count. Its generated default working hours are 07:00-19:00. Valid reservations fit both daily work periods and team boundaries.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.precedence: Group/department override replaces the category choice. Generated shift definitions supply times; custom per-task weekly hours take precedence for work periods. The existing category pool stores its effective roster pattern.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.editor_behaviour: New category templates use none. Recognised four-on-four-off aliases normalise to four_on_four_off_12h; unknown identifiers normalise to none. Dialogs offer the two patterns.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.validation: Independent raw/editor reference tests cover both patterns and group overrides, exact boundaries, travel deferral, overnight service and impossible travel. Unknown strings remain coerced rather than rejected.
task_generation.categories.*.staff_shift.limitations: Custom work_days/rest_days are retained but do not alter the fixed four-day team function. Mixed patterns in a category, generator release-spreading semantics and all shift-input scalar validation remain open. Working-hours fallback records do not prove valid shift capacity.

task_generation.staff_config.shift_patte.meaning: Start of the global daily staff work period, attached to generated tasks including unspecified legacy staff choices.
task_generation.staff_config.shift_patte.precedence: Selected category/group pattern chooses the global definition. Custom per-task weekly hours override it at runtime. Static legacy tasks without these generated fields retain all-day availability.
task_generation.staff_config.shift_patte.editor_behaviour: Known global definitions are filled and normalised during import; generated reference behavior agrees before and after editor normalisation.
task_generation.staff_config.shift_patte.validation: Independent default/custom fixed-hour references cover starts, ends, weekday deferral and return completion. Existing normalisation/coercion remains; comprehensive rejection of malformed time/day values is not established.
task_generation.staff_config.shift_patte.limitations: Fixed scheduled releases are not moved by attaching hours; staff handling waits after arrival. Global enabled/release-spreading semantics and all rotating/custom interactions require separate review. Explicitly flagged working-hours fallback is not verified capacity.
